2. In this case on behalf of accused Md. Shahidul Islam, Abul Kashem and Samaruddin the learned Advocate Mr. Md. Nurul Hoque made his submissions. On behalf of the petitioner the learned Advocate Mr. S.S. Halder made his submissions and on behalf of the State the learned Advocate Mr. S.B. Barua made his submissions. 

 3. The facts of the case, in short, are that on 8.6.88 First Information Report was lodged at Araihazar P.S. by Sukumar Chandra Das, son of the petitioner and elder brother of the victim girl Miss. Ranjana Rani Das against Md. Shahidul Islam, Abul Baten, Abul Kashem, Samaruddin and 5 others under sections 366, 379, 447 of the Penal Code and under section 4(b) of the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance, 1983 read with the Special Powers Act, 1974 alleging as follows:- 

 The present petitioner (father of the victim girl) submitted a certificate of the Head Master of the Sultan Sadi High School showing that her date of birth being 11.9.71 she is a minor aged 16 years 10 months. On behalf of the petitioner Sukhendra Das reference was made to the Majority Act, 1875 the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 and Child Marriage Restraint Act 1929 (as amended in 1984) and it was submitted that her alleged conversion to Islam is illegal, unlawful and ab initio void that she being a Hindu minor is not legally competent in law to give any consent to any marriage with a Muslim boy and as such she should be released in the custody of her petitioner father. The Sessions Judge by his order directed that the victim girl Ranjana Rani Das alias Shahida Begum should be kept in judicial custody as Advocate Suraiya Chowdhury submitted that she would not keep the said girl in her custody any more. The learned Sessions Judge by his order dated 3.8.88 asked the Director General of Health to take necessary steps for determination of the age of the victim girl. At this stage present Rule was issued on 21.8.88 and it was ordered by this Court on that date the proceedings in criminal misc. case No. 744 of 1988 in the court of Sessions Judge, Narayanganj may proceed except that the victim girl Ranjana Rani Das should not be released from custody. Thereafter a medical report signed by three professors of the Dhaka Medical College dated 15.10.88 was received by the Sessions Judge stating that they were of the view on examination of her person and X-ray film that her age was between 18 and 19 years. On 6.11.88 the Sessions Judge granted bail to accused' Md. Shahidul Islam, Abul Kashem, Nuru Miah, Serajul Islam, Fazlul Huq and Abdus Salam but strangely did not direct them to surrender before the court of Upazila Magistrate, Araihazar in whose court the said case is pending. The Sessions Judge by his order dated 6.11.88 made following uncalled  for observations beyond his jurisdiction, prejudicing the trial; 

 The record of the court of Upazila Magistrate, Araihazar is not before us. Presumably the Upazila Magistrate Araihazar issued search warrant under section 100 Cr.P.C. for the recovery of the victim girl Ranjana Rani Das. It appears that on 19.7.88 accused Md. Shahidul Islam, Nurul Islam, Nuru Miah, Serajul Islam. Fazlul Huq and Abdul prayed for anticipatory bail in Criminal Misc. Case No. 744 of 1988 in the Court of Sessions Judge, Narayanganj. In the said Criminal Misc. Case No. 744 of 1988 Ranjana Rani Das assuming the name of Mst. Shahida Begum appeared before the Sessions Judge, Narayanganj along with her engaged Advocate Ansadur Rahman by filing a petition praying for releasing her in the custody of her alleged husband accused Md. Shahidul Islam. It further appears that the victim girl has also engaged Advocate Suraiya Chowdhury and Jotsna Rani Shaha. The Sessions Judge, Narayanganj first ordered on 19.7.88 that the victim girl Ranjana Rani Das alias Shahida Begum should remain in the custody of her Advocate Suraiya Chowdhury. On 19.7.88 on behalf of Ranjana Rani Das alias Shahida Begum a certificate granted by the Civil Surgeon, Narayanganj was produced showing that in the opinion of the said Civil Surgeon Ranjana Rani Das alias Shahida Begum is aged about 19 to 20 years. On 21.7.88 on behalf of RanjanaRani Das alias Shahida Begum a certificate of the Head Master of Sultan Sadi High School was filed before the Sessions Judge, Narayanganj showing Ranjana Rani Das's date of birth to be 12.9.7L On the same date 21.7.88 Ranjana Rani Das's father present petitioner Sukhendra Chandra Das submitted a petition before the learned Sessions Judge in the said Criminal Misc. Case No. 744 of 1988 stating that his daughter Ranjana Rani Das was a minor girl born on 12.9.71 as rightly recorded in the register of the Sultan Sadi High School and also in the Admit Card of S.S.C. Examination of the. Dhaka Board field in 1988. On behalf of Ranjana Rani Das alias Shahida Begum an affidavit sworn before a Notary Public on 2.6.88 was produced before the Sessions Judge, Narayanganj. It was stated by her in the said affidavit that on 2.6.88 she had voluntarily become Muslim by embracing the religion of Islam. She produced a Kabinnama before the Sessions Judge, Narayanganj showing that she was married to accused Md. Shahidul Islam on 19.6.88. The Sessions Judge, Narayanganj instead of allowing the Magistrate to take a view first himself on 18.7.88 took the primafacie view that if her date of birth is 11th September, 1971 as recorded in her school, then she is a minor girl aged about 17 years under the Majority Act. 1875 read with the Guardians and Wards Act, 1980 (Act VIII of 1890). Under the Majority Act, 1875 Ranjana Rani Das does not become a major before attaining the age of 18 years which she will attain on 11th   September, 1989. Ranjana Rani Das refused to go to the custody of her father claiming herself to be a major aged 22 years and wanted to go with her alleged husband accused Md. Shahidul Islam. The learned Sessions Judge, Narayanganj in such circumstances sent her to the judicial custody on 21.7.88 as Advocate Janaba Suraiya Chowdhury declined to keep Ranjana Rani Das any longer in her custody. The learned Sessions Judge on receipt of the report dated 15.10.88 of the Board of three professors of Dhaka Medical College (consisting of Prof. Muksudur Rahman. Department of Pathology, Prof. Majibur Rahman, Department of Forensic Medicine and Prof. Nurjahan Begum, Prof. of Gynaecologiy) to the following effect: 

 It appears that no ossification test was made by the said Board of doctors. The Sessions Judge on 6.11.88 considered the question of age of the victim girl. Ranjana Rani Das and accepted the age of Ranjana Rani Das to be 18 to 19 years as opined by the said three doctors. It appears that as this Court directed on 21.8.88 at the time of issuance of the Rule that the proceeding in Misc. Case No. 744 of 1988 of the Court of Sessions Judge, Narayanganj may continue except that Ranjana Rani Das should not be released from judicial custody the Sessions Judge, Narayanganj did not pass any fresh order regarding the custody of the victim girl. 

 6. Undisputedly Ranjana Rani Das is not an accused in this case. The only provision of law which is applicable in the matter of keeping her in judicial custody in jail is section 100 Cr.P.C. which reads as follows:- 

 "100. If any Metropolitan Magistrate, Magistrate of the first class or sub-Divisional Magistrate has reason to belive that any person is confined under such circumstance that the confinement amounts to an offence, he may issue a search warrant, and the person to whom such warrant is directed may search for the person so confined; and such search shall be made in accordance therewith, and the person, if found, shall be immediately taken before a Magistrate, who shall make such order as in the circumstances of the case seems proper". 

 The Sessions Judge, Narayanganj in the instant case being only a court of revisional jurisdiction ought to have sent the victim girl Ranjana Rani Das to the Court of Upazila Magistrate, Araihazar for passing necessary order in the matter of prime facie determination of her age and also in the matter of her custody. Instead of doing that the Sessions Judge for reasons best known to him at first kept her in the custody of her Advocate Mrs. Suriya Chowdhury which in the facts of present case amounted to allowing her to remain wherever she liked and when the Advocate after a few' days did not agree to keep Ranjana Rani Das in her custody any more, the Sessions a Judge ordered that she should be kept in judicial custody in Narayanganj Jail though Mr. Habibur Rahman the Sessions Judge knew that the victim girl Ranjana was required in the Court of the Upazila Magistrate, Araihazar and not in his court. Thereafter the victim girl's father petitioner Sukhendra Chandra Das obtained this Rule under section 491 Cr.P C. from this court. In the fact and circumstances of this case the Sessions Judge, Narayanganj on the very day of the appearance of the victim girl in his court should have straight away sent her in Police custody to be produced in the Court of the Upazila Magistrate Araihazar. 

 7. In view of G.R. case No. 51 of 1988 arising out of Araihazar P.S. case No. 2 (6) 88 pending in the Court of the Upazila Magistrate, Araihazar Upazila and in the facts of the present case there is no dispute regarding the fact that prima facie the court of the Upazila Magistrate, Araihazar has "reasons to believe that any person (victim girl) is confined (by accused Shahidul Islam and others) under such circumstances that the confinement amount to an offence" which attracts the provision of section 100 Cr.P.C. In the case of Miss Puma Chowdhury alias Bulbuli, now named Meherunness Begum Vs. The State reported in 8 DLR 393 a Division Bench consisting of B. Zaman and Hasan, 11 of the then Dacca High Court held that as the girl was major, her movement cannot be restricted and that on the said ground of majority of the girl the Magistrate was directed to release the petitioner girl at once. The same view was taken in the case of Bhola Nath Goshami Vs. The Commissioner of Police, Calcutta and others, 41 C.W.N. 333 by a Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court and therein it was observed "The question for decision is whether section 100 Cr.P.C. empowers a Magistrate to order the detention of a person who is sujuris. The words "shall make such order as in the circumstances of the case seems proper" do not vest in the Magistrate any such jurisdiction" In the case of Jai Dayal Dhingra Vs. Mt. Sohagan reported in A.I.R. 1934 Lahore 647 it was held that it is not proper that the questions involving status of parties, i.e. validity of marriage and conversion should be decided in an application in the nature of Writ of habeas corpus under section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In the case of Ayesha Begum alias Anila Chanda Vs. The State, 13 DLR a Division Bench consisting of S.M. Morshed and Salauddin Ahmed, JJ. of the then Dhaka High Court observed as follows :- 

 "We Should not be understood to have laid down that a Magistrate cannot pass under proper circumstances, acting under the provision of section 100 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, an order that a person who has been wrongfully confined, be kept in custody of the Court for a reasonable period of time in a neutral home or any other place with a view to ascertain what the free will of the person concerned is. Such a course is usually taken in order to enable such a person to be free from any coercion or influence that might have been exercised over him or her. It is thought that such person in such situation is not capable of exercising an independent mind unless kept for a reasonable fine in neutral custody. Even in such a case the person concerned cannot be detained indefinitely." 

 8. It is alleged in the F.I.R.by informant Sukumar Das, elder brother of the victim girl that his minor sister Ranjana Rani Das (aged about 17 years) was kidnapped or abducted by the accused persons with intent that she may be compelled or knowing it to be likely that she will be compelled to marry any person against her will. In the case of Md. Sayeedul Arefin Vs. Y.O. Gorfin A.I.R. 1916 (Privy Council) 242 the question of the age came up for consideration and therein Lord Shaw observed:- 

 In the case of Moru Devi Vs. The State or Kerala, A.I.R. 1958, Kerala 8 it has been observed that the medical evidence as to age of person cannot be utilised to override the effect of other cogent evidence on the point. In the case of Chato Vs, Jevindram Kutti, A.I.R. 1958 Kerala 121 delivering the judgment of the Division Bench Koshy, C.J. rejected the opinion of the Radiologist and preferred the other evidence on the point observing as follows:- 

 9. In the instant case the Civil Surgeon, Narayangang is said to have opined that the victim girl is aged between 18 to 19 years. The Board consisting of three professors of the Dhaka Medical College opined after a superficial examination of the body and the X-ray that the age of the victim girl is between 18 and 19 years. From the S.S.C. Admit Card of the Dhaka Board for the year 1988 it is found that the date of birth of the victim girl is undisputedly noted as 11.9.71. The Head Master of Sultan Sadi Govt. Primary School and the Head Master of Sultan Sadi High School stated in their certificates dated 8.8.88 and 25.6.88 respectively (Annexures B and C) that the date of birth of the victim girl Ranjana Rani Das has been noted in their school register as 11.9.71. The petitioner Sukhendra Chandra Das, father of the victim girl and Saraswati Dasi (45), mother of the victim girl have stated in their separate affidavits that Ranjana Rani Das was born on 11.9.71 in the house of petitioner Sukhendra Chandra Das in village Sultan Sadi. On basis of the affidavits made by the father and mother of Ranjana Rani Das and the date of birth noted in the registers of the Sultan Sadi Primary School and the Sultan Sadi High School and the S.S.C. Admit Card of 1988 we take the view prima facie that the date of birth of the victim girl is 11.9.71 which means that she is aged about 17 years and has not yet attained the age of 18 years. Although it is not material here yet by the way it may be mentioned that under The Child Marriage Restraints Act, 1929 (as amended by Ordinance No. XXXVIII of 1984) marriage of a girl below the age of 18 years and of a boy below the age, of twenty one years has been made a punishable offence. Under the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 read with the Majority Act 1875 any person (male or female) below the age of eighteen years is a minor for the purposes of guardianship of minor's person and property. 

 In the matter of guardianship and custody of the person of a minor the court may put the minor in the custody of an appropriate person for the minor's welfare or may keep the minor in neutral custody. We find that the victim girl Ranjana Rani Das is prima facie a minor below the age of eighteen. There is no neutral home in this country where she could be kept till she attains the age of majority or till the trial of the presest case is over whichever is earlier. In the case of Profulla Kamal Bhattacharya Vs. Ministry of Home Affairs, Govt. of Bangladesh 28 DLR (H.C) 123 it was held: 

 "The only question for determination in this case is the age of the detenu, for if the girl is minor the person best entiled to her custody will be her father, the petitioner, as the interest of the girl herself will also have to be taken into consideration in the light of the Guardians and Wards Act 1890. We asked her (Shipra Rani Bhattacharya) whether she will return to her father's custody, she refused. But the minor's refusal is not material so far as her custody is concerned. The father is certainly the best well-wisher of his daughter and in her own interest she should go into her father's custody". 

 10. In the case of Kiran Bala Choudhury Vs. the State reported in 17 DLR (Dacca) 544 a Division Bench of the then Dacca High Court directed that the detenu who was a minor girl should be made over to the custody of her mother since she (the minor girl) should not be left in the street. 

 11. In the present case it has been stated above that prima-facie at this stage we take the view that she is a minor aged about 17 years born on 11.9.71. This view will not prejudice the other party at the trial and the trial court will be at liberty to determine the age on the basis of evidence. As the victim girl Ranjana Rani Das prima-facie appears to be aged about 17 years born on 11.9.71 it is in the best interest of the victim girl that she remains in the custody of her father petitioner Sukhendra Chandra Das as the said father is the greatest well-wisher of the victim girl. She is at liberty to go wherever she likes when she attains the age of majority. 

 13. From perusal of the papers filed by the parties it is found that the Sessions Judge, Narayanganj while dealing with the matter of anticipatory bail of the accused persons granted them ad-interim bail on 6.4.88 in Criminal Misc. Case No. 744 of 1988, but has not directed them to appear before the Upazila Magistrate, Araihazar within a date fixed by him as the said court of Upazila Magistrate is the competent Court to try the C.R.Case No. 51 of 1988 arising out of Araihazar P.S. Case No. 2 (6) 88. The Sessions Judge, Narayanganj is hereby directed to ask the Accused (1) Shahidul Islam, (2) Nurul Islam (3) Nuru Mia, (4) Serajul Islam, (5) Fazlul Huq, (6) Abdul, (7) Abdus Salam and (8) Abul Kashem to surrender before the Upazila Magistrate, Araihazar on a date fixed by him as they are still fugitives from justice in that court of the Upazila Magistrate Araihazar. Let a copy of this judgment be sent at once to the Sessions Judge and the Deputy Commissioner, Narayanganj and also to the Upazila Magistrate Araihazar Upazila.
